## (1) The rows, one by one

(`hardening-inventory.md` lines 1440 – 1448) were read whole. Each pin was re-killed by this seat's own mutant(s).
"KILLED" means the run exited 1 and the first failing test is the row's pin, named in the log
`/tmp/…/scratchpad/mut/logs/<id>.log` (summarised below).

**Row 1 — the runner judges the thread a leg's answer names.** `answers.test.ts` (new) hands `runCrossHost` a Node leg
stub as the fixture's Node bundle. The stub answers on the wrong thread; every run must be `failed` with
`crossHostThreadProblem`'s reason, verbatim. A control (the right thread) must run, and a silent stub must be killed at
`timeoutMs` with `no answer within 1500 ms`. `browser-stub.test.ts` (new) does the same for the browser leg's page answer,
through a `vi.mock('playwright-core')` stub. No browser runs and no cell is faked into a report.

| mutant | change | result |
|---|---|---|
| C01 | the Node leg's `checkThread` call made `null` (= note 1's M17) | KILLED by answers.test.ts "a leg answering on the wrong thread is failed …" |
| C02 | the browser leg's `checkThread` call made `null` | KILLED by browser-stub.test.ts "a page answering on the wrong thread …" |
| C03 | the Node leg's mismatch reason replaced by `'thread mismatch'` | KILLED by answers.test.ts (the reason is pinned verbatim) |
| C04 | the browser leg's mismatch run pushed `blocked`, not `failed` | KILLED by browser-stub.test.ts |
| C34 | the Node kill timer's reason replaced by `'killed'` | KILLED by answers.test.ts "a leg that never answers is killed at the time limit …" |
